speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) how many Singapore-based companies have cumulatively invested in the Government's overseas industrial park projects that enjoy G-to-G support, such as the Suzhou Industrial Park and Tianjin Eco-City; (b) how many of these are GLCs, SMEs and MNCs respectively; and (c) what evidence has been accumulated by the Ministry as to the spin-off benefits to the domestic economy and local SMEs of these Government-supported overseas industrial parks.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Government-to-Government (G-to-G) projects, such as the Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP), Tianjin Eco-city (TEC), Chongqing Connectivity Initiative and the Amaravati Capital City project in Andhra Pradesh, play an enabling role in paving the way for Singapore companies to enter and scale up in fast-growing markets, such as China and India.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Over the years, many Singapore companies have tapped on these G-to-G platforms to go abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Of these, approximately 70% are small companies with registered capital of up to S$1 million.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The National University of Singapore has also established a research institute, the NUS (Suzhou) Research Institute (NUSRI), in SIP which has served as a springboard for Singapore startups to incubate and scale up in China.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Just to give Members an example of a company that has benefited from SIP and scaled successfully is PatSnap, founded in 2007, a Singapore company that offers innovative patent data analytics solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, to overcome the small domestic market constraints, they scaled up by first going overseas to SIP and today their software has been sold in over 40 countries to more than 1,300 clients.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In March this year, the company announced its plans to invest S$22 million in a research and development (R&D) centre in Singapore to further develop its intelligence platform.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To date, the centre has hired more than 10 data scientists.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The TEC project was established in 2008, against the backdrop of rapid urbanisation and heightened focus on sustainable economic development in China.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Companies include small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in a range of sectors, such as environmental services, property, education, urban solutions and logistics.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Singapore’s newer G-to-G projects continue to bring our companies to new regions and markets to help them gain a first-mover advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Chongqing Connectivity Initiative project, which was launched in 2015, has opened up business opportunities in the less developed western region of China, and facilitates the participation of Singapore companies in sectors, such as financial services, aviation, transport and logistics, and information and communications technology.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Similarly, the Amaravati project to build a new capital city in Andhra Pradesh will give Singapore companies the opportunity to export our expertise in urban solutions and other domains.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: With our early involvement in the initiative, our companies, including SMEs, will be well-positioned to offer their services and participate in projects within the state of Andhra Pradesh as well as in the broader Indian market.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Of the 42 companies, would the Minister have the proportion which are SMEs?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And then the second question is really on whether the Ministry of Trade and Industry has studied the issue of the impact of these investments on domestic operations and what is the positive feedback loop?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, to what extent are domestic operations impacted and in what way, from these investments overseas, whether there is any study or any data in that regard?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just wanted to know the 42 companies in TEC.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: What proportion are SMEs, if the Minister has that data?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In general, when companies go overseas, they do not just do it on their own.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The larger question is whether there is a value proposition back to Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is where what I have emphasised earlier and which is worth repeating, whether it is through G-to-G projects or through other initiatives to take our companies overseas, or free trade agreements and other initiatives to help our companies internationalise, what is the fundamental objective?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I gave Members the example of the patent company where they are doing R&D in Singapore that creates 10 new jobs which were not there before.
